rows.en: The EX-Gear has three main modes.
You can switch freely between Walk mode, Hover mode and Flight mode with the analog stick.
Analog stick down switches to Walk mode, left or right to Hover mode, and up to Flight mode.
Each mode has its own controls, but basically you move with up, down, left and right on the D-pad.
For example, in Walk mode, up and down on the D-pad move you forward and back, and left and right move you sideways.
I'll explain each mode's own controls later. First, practice switching modes.
All right, let's begin the explanation.
Sigh... I'll explain it, so listen properly!
Practice hard until you can move freely.
Next, we'll do Walk mode training.
Next, we'll do Hover mode training.
Next, we'll do Flight mode training.
Next, we'll do melee attack training.
Next, we'll do shooting attack training.
Next, we'll do cargo hauling training.
Walk mode training is over.
Hover mode training is over.
Flight mode training is over.
Melee attack training is over.
Shooting attack training is over.
Cargo hauling training is over.
Step outside the room and training is over.
Leave this room and training will end.
Press the L button to turn the camera toward your direction of travel.
Thank you.
We cannot allow the culture of the Protoculture to be lost.
rows.notes: Exsedol's formal register (-mairimasen).

rows.en: Hmm. I have no record of that type in my memory, I'm afraid.

rows.notes: A drawn-out sigh or exclamation (haa); Whisper low confidence.

rows.en: Oh! The Protodeviln!
rows.notes: Transcript has purotodebiru; read as Protodeviln (purotodebirun), glossary spelling.

rows.en: You're pretty good yourself.
I can do that much too!
This is getting dangerous!
rows.notes: 210-217: lines to the partner.

rows.en: Shouldn't you fall back for now?!
Get it together!
They got you?!
You're kidding! You got shot down?!
Damn it! This is because I wasn't good enough!
I can't fall behind either.
Whoa! What skill!
A Konig Monster...
rows.notes: keenihhi monsutaa; Konig Monster as the glossary/MUF voice lines (no o-umlaut in the font). No context for the tone (stock line in 13 missions).

rows.en: This song... Ranka... you...
rows.notes: Transcript has nanka between the pauses; read as Ranka (the MUF clip pf_alt/629 has the same mishearing).

rows.en: Idiot! It's dangerous here! Get to a shelter, quick!
Ranka!
rows.notes: Transcript nanka; read as Ranka (same mishearing as row 3241, episode 1 sequence).

rows.en: Stay still!
rows.notes: Transcript jikkou shite ro ('keep executing'); read as jitto shite ro ('stay still').

rows.en: I can do this!
Armored?!
rows.notes: Transcript amado; read as aamaado (Armored Pack), as in row 3250. No context to confirm.

rows.en: I-I'm... Never mind that, what the hell is this monster?! Why?!
rows.notes: Longer take of pf_alt/600 ('What the hell is this monster?! Why?!').

rows.en: I'll beat your record in no time.
Damn you! You cranked up the enemy difficulty!
rows.notes: Simulator training (Michel runs it, pf_mcl/1000).

rows.en: In that heavy Armored Pack...
rows.notes: Transcript amado; read as aamaado (Armored), Alto chasing an Armored Valkyrie in the Galaxy rescue. Unfinished sentence continues in row 3251.

rows.en: Like I'll just sit back and fall behind!
rows.notes: Transcript hanasarete damaru ka yo; possibly hanasarete tamaru ka yo ('no way I'm falling behind'); both give this sense.
Battle shout (haa!).

rows.en: That's Sheryl's concert venue!
rows.notes: raibu = concert (terms.json).

rows.en: You'll get killed!
rows.notes: Transcript only shinu! (low confidence); read as a warning (shinu zo!). Could be Alto about himself ('I'll die!').

rows.en: Stop it!
Ranka!
Damn Vajra! Why Ranka?!
rows.notes: Transcript doushite nanka wo; read as doushite Ranka wo.

rows.en: Backup? Antares 1?
rows.notes: Transcript antarusu wante; read as Antares 1 (callsign as py_blr/001).

rows.en: Roger.
Ranka!
rows.notes: Transcript rakkaa; read as Ranka.

rows.en: Warrant Officer Alto Saotome, S.M.S. Skull Squadron, to Antares 1. Thank you for your support.
rows.notes: Transcript juin read as jun'i (Warrant Officer, Alto's S.M.S. rank as I recall it, not in the glossary); kikan ('engine') read as kikan ('you', to an officer).

rows.en: Let's wrap this up fast.
rows.notes: 1030-1039: mock battle with Michel.

rows.en: Why do I have to do this?
That should do it.
That much should be plenty.
Just so you know, I won't hold back.
What?! Quit screwing around!
Next time, we settle this!
I was so close...
I win, Michel!
rows.notes: The Japanese says Misheru: 'Michel' per the glossary. Existing pf_alt lines in voice.json write 'Michael' for Misheru.

rows.en: I've still got a long way to go.
Sheryl, Ranka, you both explained things well.
rows.notes: 1100-1103: end of tutorial MT_050, Alto as the student of Sheryl and Ranka (12 tutorial lessons).

rows.en: But I understood nine of your explanations. The other three... sorry.
rows.notes: Transcript 9-tsu made rikai dekita kedo, 3-tsu wa; taken literally (12 tutorials MT_010-MT_050).

rows.en: Huh? But I missed the important explanations...
rows.notes: Trails off in the Japanese.

rows.en: So I just need to hear the explanations again?
Well, looks like it's my turn to shine.
rows.notes: Bobby: feminine, flamboyant register (onee-kotoba) in the calm lines, rough in battle shouts.

rows.en: Here we gooo!
The battlefield is calling for me, darling.
Too soft!
Too slow!
